verdict.rationale: Obsidian's core app runs entirely on the user's own device. Notes are local plain-text Markdown files that work offline, and the user fully controls them (obsidian-docs-2, obsidian-docs-20, obsidian-docs-23). Users can also bring their own sync via Git, Dropbox and similar tools (obsidian-docs-19), so the core product needs no vendor servers. However, the evidence documents no self-hostable server deployment. Sync and Publish are vendor-run cloud services (obsidian-docs-12, obsidian-docs-22, obsidian-docs-32), and the app is closed-source (obsidian-comm-12). Missing for 10: a self-hostable server or deployment option, self-hosted Sync or Publish, and source availability for running your own instance.
